title: Quickspin SDK Onramp Labs Journal
content:
Purpose and context:

This is a working lab-journal for the "quickspin" approach to SDK onramp. Goal is to create a small, repeatable set of labs (3–6 total) that get an engineer from zero to a production-smoke-test in under an hour while collecting the minimum telemetry to detect integration regressions.

Why "quickspin"?
- Emphasis on tight feedback loops: short exercises that exercise network, auth, streaming, and error handling in isolation.
- Labs are intentionally composable: each adds a capability and a guardrail.
- Lower cognitive overhead: each lab has a 1-line objective, 3 steps, and a 2-minute failure checklist.

Audience:
- Experienced backend/frontend engineers who need to integrate Redwood SDKs into product flows.
- Developer advocates running workshops.

High-level lab list (proposed):
1) Hello-API: CLI token + one-line generation
   - Objective: confirm credentials and basic request/response.
   - Steps: install SDK, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run hello-gen sample.
   - Smoke checks: 200 response, tokens billed non-zero, content not empty.

2) Stream-and-cancel: streaming endpoints + early cancel behavior
   - Objective: see streaming chunk flow and validate client-side cancel semantics.
   - Steps: start streaming sample, cancel after first chunk, validate partial output and that server traces show canceled=true.
   - Failure triage: hung client => check client event loop; no chunks => check model selection (small model may not stream).

3) Auth/Rotate: key rotation + edge-case caching
   - Objective: demonstrate rotating keys without restarting app and observe telemetry delta.
   - Steps: swap key in env, hit endpoint, verify new token in logs.
   - Notes: include KMS HSM stub for Private customers.

4) Local-mode hermeticization: offline stubbing and network jitter
   - Objective: run SDK tests with hermetic stubs that mimic Redwood responses and latency jitter.
   - Steps: run local stub server, run unit tests against stub, simulate 200–800ms jitter.
   - Gotcha: ensure retry/backoff mirrors production policy.

5) Prefix-caching & perf check: KV cache + token efficiency
   - Objective: show how prefix caching reduces token usage for repeated prompts.
   - Steps: run repeated prompt workload, toggle cache on/off, compare token counts in telemetry.
   - Metrics to record: tokens_per_request, latency_p50/p95, cache_hit_rate.

6) Canary rollback scenario: model downgrade + graceful fallback
   - Objective: run a small canary with a new model, trigger synthetic regression, observe automatic fallback mechanics.
   - Steps: configure canary route, send synthetic prompts, flip error flag, confirm fallback to baseline model.
   - Observability: trace link, per-route error budget.

Lab structure template (must be used for each lab):
- title (1 line)
- objective (1 line)
- estimated time (minutes)
- prerequisites (SDK version, credentials, OS)
- 3 step walkthrough (copy-paste friendly)
- quick verification (3 checks)
- failure checklist (3 items)
- telemetry assertions (what to look for in console/console dashboard)

Telemetry minimal set (for onramp):
- request_id (trace link)
- sdk_version
- model_id
- tokens_in, tokens_out, tokens_billed
- latency_ms (p50/p95)
- error_code / error_reason
- cache_hit boolean or cache_hit_rate

Quick heuristics and triage notes:
- If p95 latency >> local dev latency: check network egress region, route policy, and model selection.
- If tokens_billed unexpectedly large: confirm prompt construction (no accidental system message duplication), check reuse of prompt templates.
- If streaming fails intermittently: increase client-side receive buffer and instrument resend/cancel flow.

Workshop checklist for 25-person session:
- Pre-provisioned API keys: 25 keys mapped to seats (rotate after workshop)
- Dockerized local stub image available on GH package for offline labs
- Leader runbook: common error diag steps, slides with 1-minute demos per lab
- Telemetry dashboard template: token burn chart + per-key error heatmap

Developer ergonomics ideas to test (experiments):
- One-command lab runner: `npx redwood-quickspin run 2` to run lab 2 locally with minimal setup.
- Guided sample in IDE: generate a small code lens that inserts the hello-gen snippet and runs it in integrated terminal.
- Tiny telemetry badge: show "last 24h tokens" inside sample-app README via GH Actions.

Open questions / decisions to capture:
- Minimum SDK surface for "quickspin" — do we require chat+function calling in v1 or limit to text gen + streaming?
- How opinionated should lab defaults be about caching/autobatching? (pros: better perf; cons: hides tradeoffs)
- Should we include a pre-wired SSO flow for enterprise/on-prem tests or keep workshop keys simple?

Notes-to-self / rough TODOs:
- Draft lab 1 step-by-step with exact CLI commands and expected output (next 2 days).
- Create Docker stub image and publish to internal GH package registry (owner: Liam).
- Wire quick telemetry dashboard template (Marisol) and make copyable JSON for Console import.
- Run 2 internal dry-runs with SRE and DevX and capture timing.

Useful links (to be expanded):
- Confluence index for SDK onramp (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEV/SDK+onramp+index
- Quick telemetry dashboard draft: https://grafana.internal.redwood/board/telemetry-quickspin
- GH template for labs: https://github.com/redwood-ai/sdk-labs/tree/quickspin

Signature:
Asha P. (DevX) — initial quickspin journal. Updates will be appended as we iterate through dry runs and workshop feedback.

Quick log:
- 2025-11-15: spin 0 — outline and lab list created.
- 2025-12-02: prototyped hello-gen and stream-cancel; streaming behavior inconsistent in node 18.15.
- 2026-01-12: added auth/rotate lab notes and KMS stub suggestion.
- 2026-02-25: integrated telemetry assertions and workshop checklist; moved to broader dry-run planning.

(End of journal entry)
